key_insight: A combined CEL simulation and ANN framework can accurately predict friction stir welding quality in HDPE and identify process windows that reduce defects while stabilizing heat and force responses.
engineering_relevance: The study provides practical guidance for selecting rotational speed, welding speed, and preheating conditions to produce stronger, more reliable thermoplastic welds with fewer voids and wormholes.
method: 3D coupled Eulerian-Lagrangian (CEL) model of the FSW process
Two multilayer perceptron ANNs trained on experimental temperature and axial-force data
Process map generation to distinguish defect-free and defective welding windows
evidence_signal: The ANN models achieved high predictive performance with R2 values between 0.91 and 0.99, and the CEL model matched experimental observations of thermal, mechanical, and defect behavior.
watch_item: The framework was validated on a limited parameter space, so performance and recommended settings may need rechecking for other HDPE grades, tool geometries, or larger-scale production conditions.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
